course_name_original: Selección de materiales y fabricación de medios de producción
course_name_en: Materials Selection and Manufacturing of Production Means
prerequisites: Ciencia y tecnología de los materiales/V12G380V01301
Fundamentos de sistemas y tecnologías de fabricación/V12G380V01305
Ingeniería de fabricación y calidad dimensional/V12G380V01604

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the new trends in materials and their shaping processes.
Selects materials based on their physical, chemical, mechanical, thermal, electrical, and magnetic properties.
Develops material selection strategies taking into account the limits of their properties, their shaping, joining, finishing, and sustainability capabilities.
Uses databases to make decisions on the correct selection of material for a given component or structure.
Associates design possibilities with each material transformation process.
Selects, designs, and optimizes transformation processes for a material based on product design, use, and environmental impact.
Proposes innovative product solutions based on materials and their processes. Analyzes and proposes operational solutions to problems in the field of materials engineering.
Knows and values the experimental process used in manufacturing processes, as well as the necessary means and tools.
Masters the basic knowledge for the elaboration of tooling and manufacturing tool projects. Deepens knowledge of manufacturing techniques and innovations in the manufacturing of tooling and tools.

Demonstrates communication and teamwork skills. Identifies own information needs and uses available means, spaces, and services to design and execute appropriate searches for the thematic area. Carries out assigned tasks based on basic guidance from the professor, deciding the duration of the parts, including personal contributions, and expanding information sources.
learning_outcomes.code: B1 B5 B6 B8 C25 C26 D5 D9 D17

syllabus_topics: The world of materials. Different families. Characteristics.
Materials based on their mechanical properties.
Materials based on their thermal, electrical, optical and magnetic properties.
Materials based on their chemical properties.
Study of material degradation processes. Ways to prevent it.
Material selection based on environmental impact and recyclability.
Methodology for selecting the most suitable materials based on product design.
Material transformation processes for improving their service life.
Selection of materials and processes applied to products in key industrial sectors.
Electroerosion: process planning and electrode manufacturing.
Processing of wood and similar materials.
Forces and energies in different manufacturing processes.
Construction and management of material maps. Material indices.
Evaluation of degradation and protection of non-metallic materials.
Selection of materials and processes applied to products in key industrial sectors. Practical cases.
Manufacturing of parts by additive methods.
Welding: influence of parameters on the process.
Manufacturing of mechanized tooling and design of control mock-up.
teaching_methods: Lectures (combining board explanations with videos and computer presentations)
Laboratory practices (using instruments and machines, combined with computer simulations and company visits)
ICT-supported practices (using CES-Edupack software for material and process selection in the computer lab)
Project-based learning (team project integrating manufacturing and material selection, defended orally)

assessment_methods.method: Practice report, practicum, and external practices

assessment_rules: For students with continuous evaluation, the final grade is composed of an objective questions exam (40%), a practice report (10%), a project (30%), and laboratory practical exercises (20%). The objective questions exam scores 0.25 points for correct answers and subtracts 0.1 points for incorrect answers, with blank questions not scoring, and a maximum of 2 blank questions per thematic block allowed. For students without continuous evaluation, the final grade is based on an objective questions exam (40%) and an exam consisting of solving several theoretical-practical problems (60%). In both cases, to pass the course, at least 5 points (out of 10) must be obtained from the sum of all components, and for the theoretical-practical problems, it is necessary to obtain at least 1 point per thematic block. In the 2nd edition (resit), the objective test score is maintained, while the practice report and project scores can be improved by redoing the work, and laboratory practicals can be redone as a joint exercise.
